title: Reliance Industries: Decoding FY26 Dividend and AGM Impact
description: Reliance Industries' 49th Annual General Meeting (AGM) is scheduled for June 19, 2026. The record date for determining eligibility for the FY26 dividend has b.

faq.q: What is an Annual General Meeting (AGM)?
faq.a: An AGM is a mandatory yearly meeting where a company's board of directors presents its financial results to shareholders, discusses company performance, and addresses key corporate decisions. Shareholders also vote on resolutions and can ask questions to the management.

faq.q: What is a record date for dividends?
faq.a: The record date is a specific cut-off date set by a company. Only shareholders whose names appear in the company's register of members on this date are eligible to receive the declared dividend.

faq.q: How are dividends taxed in India?
faq.a: Dividends received from Indian companies are currently taxable in the hands of the individual shareholder. The dividend income is added to your total income and taxed as per your applicable income tax slab rates.

faq.q: What if I buy shares on the record date?
faq.a: If you buy shares on the record date, you will generally not be eligible for the dividend. This is because of the T+1 or T+2 settlement cycle (depending on the stock exchange and type of security). You need to purchase shares before the ex-dividend date to ensure they are credited to your demat account by the record date.

faq.q: When can I expect the dividend payment?
faq.a: Once the dividend is declared at the AGM and the record date has passed, the company typically processes the payment within 30 days of the declaration. The amount is usually credited directly to the bank account linked to your demat account.

faq.q: How does this announcement affect Reliance's share price?
faq.a: Dividend announcements and strong financial results often generate positive sentiment, which can lead to increased buying interest in the short term. However, on the ex-dividend date, the share price typically adjusts downwards by an amount roughly equivalent to the dividend per share.
